Develop a comprehensive framework for media management by efficiently transferring raw footage, cataloguing files, and categorizing content to prepare for editing.
Support the editing process of raw footage to craft engaging and polished video content tailored for a variety of platforms, including social media, websites, promotional materials, and presentations.
Collaborate with the creative team to brainstorm ideas, develop concepts, and execute projects from start to finish.
Ensure all video content aligns with the company's brand identity, style guidelines, and messaging.
Stay updated on industry trends and best practices in video editing techniques, software, and technology.
Support the production team with tasks such as organizing files, managing equipment, and coordinating schedules.
Other tasks as required.
Qualifications and Experience:
Experience working with travel vlog style content
Proficiency in video editing software such as Adobe Creative Cloud Suite, with imperative experience pertaining to Premiere Pro
Strong understanding of video production processes, including shooting, lighting, and audio recording
Excellent communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively in a team environment
Experience working with 360 cam content
Experience creating short format vertical content would be a plus
Benefits:
Competitive salary
Paid time off

Job Types: Full-time, Internship / Co-op

Toronto, ON M5V 2M5: reliably commute or plan to relocate before starting work (required)

title: Intermediate Environmental Soil & Groundwater Investigation Specialist
description:
Equilibrium
Company Description
Equilibrium is a multidisciplinary firm specializing in reducing environmental liability at contaminated sites through advanced risk assessment and remediation techniques. The company supports clients across Western Canada and internationally with Phase 1-3 investigations, standard and advanced remediation, and research funded by industry and government. Equilibrium has pioneered regulatory guideline updates such as the Subsoil Salinity Tool (SST) and engages in innovative in-situ remediation projects. The team is dynamic, creative, and committed to process efficiency.
The position is based out of the head-office in Calgary, AB (hybrid), or out of Edmonton or Lloydminster (remote). It focuses on field work across Alberta and Saskatchewan, coordinating and executing Phase 1-3 Environmental Site Assessments and groundwater characterization, with a primary emphasis on drilling and remediation activities.
Location and Work Arrangement
Hybrid remote in Calgary, Edmonton or Lloydminster.
Employment Type
Full-time
Responsibilities
Participate in the Equilibrium safety program.
Coordinate, manage, and execute field programs including Phase 1, 2, and 3 Environmental Site Assessments and groundwater characterization.
Learn and apply investigation strategies that generate data to support risk assessment studies and risk-based remediation guidelines.
Conduct field work comprising approximately 25-40 of total time.
Complete all aspects of ground disturbance for field programs, including planning, leading, and coordinating third-party contractors.
Track field data and information, provide accurate daily cost updates and other client requirements.
Complete analytical data validation and Quality Assurance/Quality Control.
Write technical reports on Phase 1, 2, and 3 activities, drill program plans, data gap and remedial action plan documents.
Apply relevant Tier 1, Tier 2, and/or Tier 3 soil and groundwater guidelines, assess exceedances, and develop Tier 2 guidelines.
Participate in novel in-situ remediation projects and advanced SST techniques.
Train and mentor junior field staff.
Work successfully as part of a multidisciplinary team, in the field, and in the office.
Required Qualifications
Minimum 5 years of experience leading environmental investigation and remediation field programs, including all aspects of ground disturbance.
Experience developing Tier 2 soil and groundwater remediation guidelines is a strong asset.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Willingness and ability to travel extensively and perform mentally and physically demanding tasks.
Field programs may involve up to 14 consecutive days.
Degree or diploma in environmental science, soil science, engineering, hydrogeology, geology, or agrology.
Preferred Qualifications
Master’s degree.
Strong spatial reasoning ability and interest in learning risk assessment techniques.
Professional designation such as Professional Agrologist, Registered Technologist in Agrology, Professional Engineer, Certified Engineering Technologist, Professional Geologist or Hydrogeologist, Professional Biologist, or Environmental Professional.
Formal experience with First Nations cultures, practices, and environmental stewardship.
Benefits and Compensation
Equilibrium offers a comprehensive benefits package, flexible work hours, and training in unique environmental sector aspects. Starting wages are competitive with significant opportunities for upward mobility in salary, position, and responsibility based on performance.
Application Process
Send resume, transcripts, references, and cover letter to jobs eqm.ca. Include in your cover letter the number of years of relevant Phase 2 and Phase 3 experience and state where you saw this posting. Applicants with less than 5 years of experience or without transcripts and a minimum of 2 references will not be considered. The position remains open until the ideal candidate is found.

title: Production Planning (Aerospace Manufacturing)
description:
Excellente opportunité pour développer sa carrière dans l’une des top entreprise Aéronautique a Montréal
À propos du poste :
Nous recherchons un(e) Planificateur(trice) de Production Analyste Chaîne d’Approvisionnement organisé(e) et analytique pour rejoindre notre équipe de fabrication. Ce rôle est essentiel pour assurer le séquencement efficace des matières premières et leur flux dans la fabrication de pièces rotatives de haute précision telles que turbines, pales, rotors et diffuseurs. Le ou la candidat(e) retenu(e) jouera un rôle clé dans l’alignement des horaires de production avec les besoins des différents centres internes et clients du marché secondaire.
Responsabilités principales :
Planification et Séquencement des Matériaux :
Assurer le séquencement adéquat des matières premières pour une ligne de fabrication spécifique afin de respecter les objectifs de production et les délais de livraison.
Coordination de la Production :
Aligner les plans du centre de fabrication avec les horaires de plusieurs centres de production et clients.
Gestion des Problèmes :
Analyser et répondre aux changements de conception ou aux problèmes de qualité pouvant affecter le séquencement de production. Ajuster les plans pour minimiser les perturbations.
Opérations Quotidiennes :
Utiliser des outils tels qu’Excel et SAP pour gérer et mettre à jour les horaires de production.
Prioriser les lancements de pièces et les inspections.
Maintenir des dates de promesse précises et s’assurer que les lignes de production sont à jour.
Collaboration et Communication :
Participer aux réunions quotidiennes de production avec les chefs d’équipe et les superviseurs.
Maintenir un haut niveau de communication par appels et courriels pour coordonner avec les parties prenantes internes.
Qualifications :
Formation en génie industriel, opérations, logistique ou administration des affaires.
Diplôme universitaire ou technique dans un domaine pertinent.
Excellentes compétences en communication requises.
0 à 2 ans d’expérience avec un stage, ou 2 à 5 ans d’expérience en opérations, planification ou logistique.
Excellent opportunity to grow your career in one of the leading Aerospace companies in Montreal
About the Role:
We are seeking a highly organized and analytical Production Planner Supply Chain Analyst to join our manufacturing team. This role is essential in ensuring the efficient sequencing and flow of raw materials for the fabrication of high-precision rotating parts such as turbines, blades, rotors, and diffusers. The successful candidate will play a key role in aligning production schedules with the demands of various internal stakeholders and aftermarket customers.
Key Responsibilities:
Material Sequencing Planning:
Ensure raw materials are properly sequenced for a specific manufacturing line to meet production targets and delivery schedules.
Production Coordination:
Align fabrication center plans with the schedules of multiple production and customer centers.
Issue Management:
Analyze and respond to design changes or quality issues that may impact production sequencing. Adjust plans to minimize disruptions.
Daily Operations:
Use tools such as Excel and SAP to manage and update production schedules.
Prioritize part releases and inspections.
Maintain accurate promise dates and ensure production lines are up to date.
Collaboration Communication:
Participate in daily production meetings with team leads and supervisors.
Maintain high levels of communication via calls and emails to coordinate with internal stakeholders.

title: Policy Analyst/Analyste des Politiques
location: for Climate Solutions / Fermiers pour la transition climatique Remote
description:
Farmers for Climate Solutions (FCS) is a national farmer- and rancher-led coalition advancing solutions that help the agriculture sector prosper in a changing climate. We offer peer-to-peer field programming that supports farmers and ranchers to adopt on-farm practices that build resilience and improve economic and environmental sustainability. We amplify farmer and rancher voices to policy-makers, industry, and financial institutions so that, together, we can build a future in which Canadian agriculture thrives.
FCS is seeking a Policy Analyst to help conduct policy research and analysis on climate and agriculture; to support the development of policy tools for advocacy (ex: reports, documents, briefings and surveys); to collaborate with members, partners, and the broader sector to inform policy priorities; and to provide background support for advocacy initiatives.
Our farmer and rancher-led, solutions-oriented approach and distinct voice are helping to build bridges and shift the needle on climate change in agriculture in Canada. This is an opportunity to work with farmer and rancher leaders and partners across the country to advance policy solutions that support high resilience, low emissions farming and ranching.
Experience we are seeking
The Policy Analyst will report to the Policy Director and will collaborate with the rest of the FCS team and with various policy advisory bodies, research task forces, and working groups.
The information below describes the Policy Analyst, and the experience/qualifications needed to succeed in the job. If you possess approximately 80 percent of the essential experience/qualifications, we encourage you to apply.
In collaboration, conduct and coordinate policy research and analysis on agriculture and climate in Canada and abroad by:
Collecting and analyzing data and research on emerging policy priorities in climate and agriculture, and summarizing relevant results for FCS policy work
Analyzing key government, industry, and international reports and publications on climate and agriculture, and synthesizing key findings for integration into FCS policy work
Providing relevant background and review to help inform FCS policy research task forces, advisory bodies, and working groups advancing research, policy tools, and advocacy strategies
Supporting the development, analysis, and dissemination of results from FCS-led polls, surveys, and other data collection tools
Experience/qualifications
ESSENTIAL
Post-secondary degree or diploma in related field
5-7 years experience in a professional environment in a related field
Strong understanding of Canadian policy, as it relates to agriculture and climate change
A strong interest in and understanding of research on climate change, agronomy, agricultural economics, and behavioural social science in agriculture
Up-to-date understanding of the diversity of Canadian agriculture, and opportunities and challenges for climate adaptation and mitigation
Experience researching, synthesizing and analyzing complex information, tailoring messages to diverse audiences, and strategically integrating research findings into policy priorities
Capacity to work in a fast-paced environment and to react quickly to new opportunities,priorities, and risks or threats
A sharp eye for detail
Ability to communicate clearly and compellingly in written and verbal English
ASSET
Ability to communicate clearly and compellingly in written and verbal French
Support the development of policy tools for advocacy by:
Supporting the drafting of policy tools like reports, briefing notes, presentations, etc.
Supporting the preparation of policy briefings for FCS members
Helping to monitor and evaluate success of advocacy tools and projects, and adapt accordingly
Experience developing policy material (briefing notes, etc.) for various audiences with clear, concise, and accessible language, while supporting the organization’s unique position and voice
Experience analyzing statistical information and integrating relevant information into policy material (reports, briefing notes, etc.)
Experience in monitoring, evaluation, and learning of policy tools and projects
Support sector engagement on policy priorities by:
Supporting the background needs and facilitation of policy working and advisory groups
Supporting relationships with key sector and industry partners and stakeholders on FCS policy priorities
Ability to work collaboratively with colleagues and partners towards a common goal
Strong skills in engaged listening and diplomacy
Demonstrated ability to build strong relationships and bridges among partners with diverse views and opinions

Solid computer skills and experience using Google Workspace and Zoom

Ability to be flexible and adapt to changing project needs and priorities
Available to travel occasionally for meetings, retreats, or trainings

Analyste des politiques, Fermiers pour la transition climatique
Fermiers pour la transition climatique (FTC) est une coalition nationale
d’agriculteur rice s et d’éleveur se s qui promeut des solutions pour aider le secteur agricole à prospérer sous des conditions climatiques changeantes. Nous offrons des programmes entre pairs sur le terrain pour aider les agriculteur rice s et les éleveur se s à adopter des pratiques à la ferme qui renforcent la résilience et améliorent la viabilité économique et la durabilité environnementale. Nous faisons en sorte que les agriculteur rice s et les éleveur se s soient entendus par les acteur rice s politiques, agricoles et financiers afin qu’ensemble, nous puissions bâtir un avenir au sein duquel l’agriculture est florissante.
FTC est à la recherche d’un e analyste des politiques pour l’aider à mener des recherches et des analyses sur les politiques climatiques et agricoles; pour soutenir l’élaboration d’outils politiques destinés au travail de sensibilisation et de plaidoyer (ex. : rapports, documents, notes d’information et enquêtes); pour collaborer avec les membres, les partenaires et l’ensemble des acteur rice s du secteur agricole afin de définir les priorités politiques; et pour offrir un soutien de base aux initiatives de représentation et de plaidoyer politique.
La perspective distincte de FTC ainsi que son approche guidée par les agriculteur rice s et les éleveur se s qui est axée sur les solutions contribuent à créer des liens et à faire progresser l’action climatique dans le secteur agricole canadien. Cet emploi est une occasion de travailler avec des agriculteur rice s et des éleveur se s ainsi qu’avec des partenaires à travers le pays afin de promouvoir des solutions politiques qui soutiennent une agriculture fortement résiliente et produisant peu d’émissions de GES.
Expérience recherchée
L’analyste des politiques relèvera de la directrice des politiques et collaborera avec le reste de l’équipe de FTC ainsi qu’avec divers organes consultatifs politiques, groupes de recherche et comités.
Les informations ci-dessous décrit le mandat de l’analyste des politiques, de même que l’expérience et les compétences nécessaires pour réussir à ce poste. Si vous possédez environ 80 de l’expérience et des compétences essentielles, nous vous encourageons à poser votre candidature.
Mandat de l’analyste des politiques
Contribuer à la réalisation et à la coordination du travail de recherche et d’analyse sur les politiques agricoles et climatiques au Canada et ailleurs dans le monde en :
Recueillant et analysant des données et des études sur les priorités politiques émergentes en matière de climat et d’agriculture, et en synthétisant les résultats pertinents pour épauler le travail politique de FTC
Analysant les publications et les rapports clés sur le climat et l’agriculture qui ont été rédigés par les intervenant e s gouvernementaux, agricoles et internationaux dans le but d’en résumer les principaux constats et de les intégrer au travail politique de FTC
Fournissant des informations et des analyses pertinentes pour guider les groupes de travail, les organes consultatifs et les comités de FTC dans leurs activités de recherche, de développement d’outils politiques et d’élaboration de stratégies de représentation et de plaidoyer politique
Soutenant l’élaboration de sondages, d’enquêtes et d’autres outils servant aux collectes de données réalisées par FTC, de même que l’analyse et la diffusion de leurs résultats
Expérience et compétences Essentielles
Diplôme d’études postsecondaires dans un domaine connexe
Cinq à sept années d’expérience au sein d’un environnement professionnel dans un domaine connexe
Solide connaissance de la politique canadienne en matière d’agriculture et de changements climatiques
Intérêt marqué pour la recherche sur les changements climatiques, l’agronomie, l’agroéconomie et les sciences du comportement appliquées au domaine de l’agriculture, et bonne connaissance de ces domaines
Connaissance de pointe concernant la diversité du secteur agricole canadien, de même que des occasions et des défis liés à l’adaptation aux changements climatiques et à l’atténuation de leurs effets

Le secteur agricole a encore beaucoup de travail à faire pour promouvoir la réconciliation et la décolonisation, l’analyse intersectionnelle, de même que les points de vue et le leadership des agriculteur trice s méritant l’équité (c’est-à-dire les jeunes agriculteur rice s, les femmes agricultrices, les agriculteur rice s en situation de handicap, les agriculteur rice s noirs, les agriculteur rice s et les pourvoyeur se s d’aliments autochtones, les agriculteur rice s de couleur, les petits agriculteur rice s et les agriculteur rice s LGBTQ+). title: Senior PCB Design Engineer - Y
description:
Key Responsibilities:
Lead the digital/analog PCB design for space environments.
Mentor and oversee junior team members and interns in PCB design.
Translate board-level requirements into a comprehensive design concept (incorporating architecture, I/Os, key components, power dissipation estimates, FPGA integration, software integration, etc.).
Collaborate closely with FPGA, software, and test designers to finalize functional concepts and streamline integration.
Complete or review the schematic capture level design.
Identify and manage technology and design risks.
Provide guidance to ensure Design for Manufacture/Test in space environments.
Supervise and review design layout constraints, parts placement, manufacturing, and assembly drawings.
Prepare or review lists of long lead items, bills of materials, and ensure parts qualifications for space.
Conduct and review circuit simulations (using tools like SPICE, Hyperlynx, ADS, etc.) and various design analyses (e.g., worst-case scenarios, FMECA).
Coordinate with various specialized teams (structural, thermal, packaging, manufacturing, quality assurance, etc.) to conduct necessary reviews for PCB component placement and layout.
Oversee board assembly and manufacturing tests.
Prepare and review various documents, including review presentations, test plans, test procedures, etc.
Lead and guide junior team members in testing, troubleshooting, and debugging complex mixed-signal boards.
Provide support for environmental and functional tests and validation for space missions.
Report progress and address issues to the program lead or manager.
Required Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or equivalent field.
Minimum of seven (7) years of experience in designing processor, digital, analog, high-speed, or mixed-signal PCBs.
Demonstrated expertise in at least one of these areas of competence.
Proficiency in coaching and supervising junior team members and interns.
Experience in design architecture and handling multidisciplinary specifications and reviews (FPGA, software, mechanical, etc.).
Proficiency in tools/software languages such as Excel spreadsheets, Python, MathCAD, Spice, Matlab, JIRA, etc.
Strong understanding of electronic circuits and communication protocols, coupled with extensive PCB design experience.
Knowledge of PCB manufacturing processes.
Exposure to mechanical packaging is a valuable asset.
Experience conducting analyses (FMECA, WCA, signal integrity, power integrity, etc.) using various tools like SPICE, ADS SiPro, Hyperlynx, etc.
